review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

4:1.sourceText: φοβηθῶμεν οὖν μή ποτε καταλειπομένης ἐπαγγελίας εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ δοκῇ τις ἐξ ὑμῶν ὑστερηκέναι.
4:1.targetText: We may fear, then, lest a promise being left of entering into His rest, anyone of you may seem to have come short,

groups.note: The actual μήποτε negative-apprehension expression is rendered lest; its two components retain the one English connector.
The actual entering infinitive is the content of the promise; English nominalizes it as of entering without an independently printed Greek of preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:2.sourceText: καὶ γάρ ἐσμεν εὐηγγελισμένοι καθάπερ κἀκεῖνοι· ἀλλ’ οὐκ ὠφέλησεν ὁ λόγος τῆς ἀκοῆς ἐκείνους μὴ συνκεκερασμένος τῇ πίστει τοῖς ἀκούσασιν.
4:2.targetText: for we also are having good news proclaimed, even as they, but the word heard did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in those who heard,

groups.note: The actual perfect passive good-news-proclaiming participle εὐηγγελισμένοι describes people who have been evangelized; LSV are having good news proclaimed retains that actual head without establishing an ongoing proclamation event or an independent source good-news noun.
The compound κἀκεῖνοι identifies and/also those people; LSV gives they after even as. Its actual people reference remains without inventing a different Greek personal pronoun.

The actual hearing/report noun ἀκοῆς qualifies word; LSV turns word of hearing into word heard. This nominal-to-participial recast retains the actual hearing head rather than relabeling it as an ακούω verb form.
The actual dative article/faith phrase gives what the word is mixed with; English with faith expresses that complete case relation without an independent Greek with word.

unmappedSource.reason: The genitive article belongs to the hearing noun; English recasts word-of-hearing as word heard without a separate article at heard.

4:3.sourceText: Εἰσερχόμεθα γὰρ εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν οἱ πιστεύσαντες, καθὼς εἴρηκεν Ὡς ὤμοσα ἐν τῇ ὀργῇ μου Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου, καίτοι τῶν ἔργων ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου γενηθέντων.
4:3.targetText: for we enter into the rest—we who believed, as He said, “So I swore in My anger, They will [not] enter into My rest”; and yet the works were done from the foundation of the world,

groups.note: The εἰ plus entry predicate forms the negative Semitic oath, literally if they will enter with an implied adverse oath consequence. LSV explicitly renders its denial as They will not enter. The whole oath constituent supports not, not an isolated lexical if=not rule.

The actual becoming/coming-to-be participle γενηθέντων describes the works existing from creation; LSV renders their completed occurrence as were done. It retains that original coming-to-be head, not a substituted ποιέω making verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:4.sourceText: εἴρηκεν γάρ που περὶ τῆς ἑβδόμης οὕτως Καὶ κατέπαυσεν ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ·
4:4.targetText: for He spoke in a certain place concerning the seventh [day] thus: “And God rested in the seventh day from all His works”;

groups.note: The actual indefinite locative adverb πού is somewhere; English in a certain place expands that one locative without separately written certain/place words.

The feminine ordinal is substantival for the seventh day in this calendrical context; English bracketed day makes its implicit nominal role explicit, not a separately printed Greek day noun at this first occurrence. The later day has its own actual noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
The repeated attributive article introduces seventh after day; English gives the seventh day with one article rather than an extra article at the ordinal.

4:5.sourceText: καὶ ἐν τούτῳ πάλιν Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου.
4:5.targetText: and in this [place] again, “They will [not] enter into My rest”;

groups.note: The substantival neuter demonstrative refers to this cited passage/location; English makes its contextual nominal head explicit as bracketed place without an independently printed τόπος noun.
The εἰ plus entry predicate is the same negative oath construction quoted in3:11 and4:3. Bracketed not expresses that whole oath denial, not an invented independent source negator.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:6.sourceText: ἐπεὶ οὖν ἀπολείπεται τινὰς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς αὐτήν, καὶ οἱ πρότερον εὐαγγελισθέντες οὐκ εἰσῆλθον δι’ ἀπείθειαν,
4:6.targetText: since then, it remains for some to enter into it, and those who first heard good news did not enter in because of unbelief—

groups.note: The actual accusative some is the subject of the entering infinitive; English for some states that same infinitival-subject relation without an independent Greek for preposition.

The actual passive good-news-proclaiming participle means those previously evangelized; LSV recasts the receiving audience as those who heard good news. The whole English hearing-news phrase belongs to that one actual announcing predicate, not an invented ακούω hearing verb.
The actual noun ἀπείθεια names disobedience/refusal to be persuaded; LSV renders unbelief in this response-to-God context. Its source head remains distinct from the different ἀπιστία noun in3:19.

4:7.sourceText: πάλιν τινὰ ὁρίζει ἡμέραν, Σήμερον, ἐν Δαυεὶδ λέγων μετὰ τοσοῦτον χρόνον, καθὼς προείρηται Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε, μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν.
4:7.targetText: again He limits a certain day, “Today,” in David saying, after so long a time, as it has been said, “Today, if you may hear His voice, you may not harden your hearts,”

groups.note: The actual determining/appointing verb ὁρίζει is rendered limits for fixing the particular day; it is not a different Greek restriction verb.
The actual perfect passive προείρηται includes the prior-saying sense, has been said before; LSV gives it has been said without a separate before adverb, retaining the actual prefixed source head.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:8.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ αὐτοὺς Ἰησοῦς κατέπαυσεν, οὐκ ἂν περὶ ἄλλης ἐλάλει μετὰ ταῦτα ἡμέρας.
4:8.targetText: for if Joshua had given them rest, He would not have spoken after these things concerning another day;

groups.note: The actual Greek name Ἰησοῦς is the Greek form used for Joshua as well as Jesus. Here the conquest/rest argument identifies Joshua; LSV Joshua faithfully retains that person, rather than replacing a different Greek name.
The actual resting/causing-to-rest verb κατέπαυσεν is transitive with them; LSV expands the causative predicate as had given them rest, without independent Greek give and rest-noun words.

The modal ἄν with the imperfect speaking verb forms the unreal consequence of the if-clause. LSV He would have spoken renders that whole counterfactual predicate, not an ordinary past or standalone ἄν=future rule.

review.note: The pinned name Ἰησοῦς/LSV Joshua correspondence and whole counterfactual construction were checked against the actual reverse interlinear for Hebrews4:8.

4:9.sourceText: ἄρα ἀπολείπεται σαββατισμὸς τῷ λαῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ.
4:9.targetText: there remains, then, a Sabbath rest to the people of God,

groups.note: The actual σαββατισμός noun designates Sabbath rest/observance; LSV Sabbath rest retains that distinct head. It is not silently relabeled as the ordinary κατάπαυσις rest noun used elsewhere in this chapter.

4:10.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς κατέπαυσεν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ, ὥσπερ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων ὁ Θεός.
4:10.targetText: for he who entered into His rest, he also rested from his works, as God from His own.

groups.note: The actual article with own is substantival for God’s own works, with God explicitly named as subject. English His own states that same owner/elliptical-work relation without a separate original His pronoun or another work noun.

4:11.sourceText: Σπουδάσωμεν οὖν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς ἐκείνην τὴν κατάπαυσιν, ἵνα μὴ ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ τις ὑποδείγματι πέσῃ τῆς ἀπειθείας.
4:11.targetText: May we be diligent, then, to enter into that rest, that no one may fall in the same example of the unbelief,

groups.note: The negative μή with indefinite anyone, τις, jointly yields no one; both actual source words share that English negative-indefinite expression.
The actual ἀπείθεια is disobedience/refusal to be persuaded, rendered unbelief by LSV; its actual lemma remains distinct from ἀπιστία.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:12.sourceText: Ζῶν γὰρ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐνεργὴς καὶ τομώτερος ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν μάχαιραν δίστομον καὶ διϊκνούμενος ἄχρι μερισμοῦ ψυχῆς καὶ πνεύματος, ἁρμῶν τε καὶ μυελῶν, καὶ κριτικὸς ἐνθυμήσεων καὶ ἐννοιῶν καρδίας·
4:12.targetText: for the Word of God is living, and working, and sharper—beyond every two-edged sword—and piercing as far as [the] division of soul and spirit, of joints and also marrows, and a discerner of thoughts and intents of the heart;

groups.note: The actual living participle ζῶν predicates life of the Word; English is living includes the auxiliary with that real verbal head, not an article or an invented finite Greek be verb.
The actual active/effective adjective ἐνεργής is rendered working; it is not a separately printed Greek working verb form.
The actual discerning/judging adjective κριτικός is substantival in LSV a discerner; it retains that real adjective head rather than a different Greek judge noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the bracketed article before division; the actual division noun is anarthrous.

4:13.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν κτίσις ἀφανὴς ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, πάντα δὲ γυμνὰ καὶ τετραχηλισμένα τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ, πρὸς ὃν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος.
4:13.targetText: and there is not a created thing hidden before Him, but all things [are] naked and open to His eyes—with whom is our reckoning.

groups.note: The actual creation/creature noun κτίσις is rendered a created thing; the English created/thing phrase belongs to that noun without an independent original creating participle or thing noun.

The actual perfect passive τετραχηλισμένα describes being laid bare/exposed, rendered open. Its written verbal predicate supports English are, shared by naked and open, without assigning a copula to the nominal naked adjective or inventing a finite be word.
Greek ἡμῖν is dative us in the account relation; LSV recasts that actual accounting participant as possessive our reckoning, without a separate original possessive form.
The actual λόγος here has its account/reckoning sense; this is the same written lemma as Word in4:12 with a different contextual use, not a substituted different Greek accounting noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in the final nominal with-whom-our-reckoning clause; the actual earlier there-is verb belongs to the different no-created-thing-hidden clause and is not moved here.

4:14.sourceText: Ἔχοντες οὖν ἀρχιερέα μέγαν διεληλυθότα τοὺς οὐρανούς, Ἰησοῦν τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, κρατῶμεν τῆς ὁμολογίας.
4:14.targetText: Having, then, a great Chief Priest having passed through the heavens—Jesus the Son of God—may we hold fast the profession,

groups.note: The actual ὁμολογία is acknowledgment/confession; LSV profession uses that declared-faith sense, not a modern job/occupation meaning.

4:15.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ἔχομεν ἀρχιερέα μὴ δυνάμενον συνπαθῆσαι ταῖς ἀσθενείαις ἡμῶν, πεπειρασμένον δὲ κατὰ πάντα καθ’ ὁμοιότητα χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας.
4:15.targetText: for we do not have a Chief Priest unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but [One] tempted in all things in like manner, [yet] without sin;

groups.note: The actual negative μή with the being-able participle δυνάμενον is condensed into unable; both real components retain that one negative ability predicate.

The actual masculine perfect passive tempted participle identifies the priest who has undergone testing; English bracketed One makes that real personal/nominal role explicit, not a new original numeral or pronoun.
The actual κατά plus likeness noun gives the comparison in like manner; both real source components retain the phrase without an invented separate manner word.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the additional adversative yet before without sin; the actual earlier δέ already belongs to the contrasting but-tempted priest designation.

4:16.sourceText: προσερχώμεθα οὖν μετὰ παρρησίας τῷ θρόνῳ τῆς χάριτος, ἵνα λάβωμεν ἔλεος καὶ χάριν εὕρωμεν εἰς εὔκαιρον βοήθειαν.
4:16.targetText: we may come near, then, with freedom, to the throne of grace, that we may receive kindness, and find grace—for seasonable help.

groups.note: The actual παρρησία denotes boldness/freedom of approach or speech; LSV freedom retains that contextual access/confidence head rather than a different liberty noun.
The actual mercy noun ἔλεος is rendered kindness; its original mercy head is retained, not a different Greek kindness noun.
